# Cache Controller Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module implements the control logic for a set-associative data cache. It accepts memory requests from the core, performs cache tag lookups, returns load data, updates cache state on stores, and forwards misses and non-cacheable accesses to the miss-handling path.

The controller is synchronous and resets asynchronously to an idle state. It is parameterizable in associativity, address field widths, cache line width, and the configured cacheable start address.

## 2. Reset and Idle Behavior

After reset, the controller must be idle and must not:

- perform cache array accesses,
- assert miss or bypass requests,
- assert grants or data-valid responses.

While idle, the controller may accept a new request. If a flush indication is active at that time, the controller must ignore the request and remain idle.

## 3. Request Acceptance

A memory request includes an address, write data, byte enables, access size, and a read/write indication. The controller responds by accepting the request and later completing it.

- A cacheable read is considered accepted when its tag lookup is started.
- A cacheable write is considered accepted when the write has been committed to the selected cache way or accepted by the miss-handling path.
- A non-cacheable or globally bypassed request is accepted immediately through the bypass path.

The controller must assert a non-idle output whenever it is not in the idle state.

## 4. Cacheable Accesses

### 4.1 Read Hit

When a cacheable load hits in the cache, the controller must return the requested 64-bit word from the matching cache line. The selected word must be the one indicated by the word-select part of the request address.

A read-data-valid response must be asserted with the returned data. If the core has already presented the next request, the controller may continue processing that next request after completing the current read. Otherwise, it must return to idle.

### 4.2 Write Hit

When a cacheable store hits in the cache, the controller must update only the way that matched. The write must modify only the byte lanes indicated by the byte enables; all other bytes in the addressed word must remain unchanged.

The addressed 64-bit word in the cache line must be replaced with the store data, and the line must be marked valid and dirty. The controller must return write acceptance once the cache array has accepted the update.

### 4.3 Read Miss

When a cacheable load misses, the controller must forward the request to the miss-handling path with all necessary attributes: address, access size, byte enables, and read/write indication.

The load must not be granted or completed until the critical word for that load is returned. When the critical word arrives, the controller must deliver it to the core together with a read-data-valid response.

While waiting for the critical word, the controller may speculatively begin looking up the next core request if one is pending. It must not grant that next request until the current load has been completed and the cache array is available.

### 4.4 Write Miss

When a cacheable store misses, the controller must forward the write miss to the miss-handling path. Once the miss-handling path accepts the write miss, the controller may consider the store complete and return write acceptance. It must not wait for the cache line refill data before completing the store.

## 5. Non-Cacheable and Bypass Accesses

An access must be treated as non-cacheable when:

- the global bypass mode is active, or
- the address is below the configured cacheable start address.

Non-cacheable accesses must not cause cache array updates and must not allocate or modify cache lines. They must be forwarded on the miss/bypass path with the bypass attribute set.

For a non-cacheable read, the returned data must come from the bypass response path. For a non-cacheable write, the controller must complete the write handshake when the bypass path accepts the request and, where applicable, when the bypass response phase completes.

## 6. Outstanding Miss Aliasing

Before issuing a miss, the controller must check whether the same cache line already has an outstanding miss. The controller must provide the relevant line address for this check.

If a match is found, the controller must not issue a duplicate miss request. Instead, it must wait until the outstanding miss is cleared. After the matching miss completes, the controller must re-evaluate the cache state for the saved request. If the line has now been filled, the request may proceed as a hit; otherwise, the controller may issue the miss again.

## 7. Flush and Kill Behavior

### 7.1 Flush

While flush is active, the controller must not start any new transaction. It must not begin speculative lookups for new requests.

Flush must not abort an already accepted transaction. A transaction that is already in progress may continue to completion.

### 7.2 Kill

If the core kills a request while the controller is still waiting for tag lookup or before the request has been forwarded to the miss/bypass path, the controller must abort that request.

A killed request must not cause any cache write, miss request, or bypass request. The controller must still produce a data-valid completion pulse so that the request can be retired.

If a request has already been forwarded to the miss/bypass path, a later kill indication shall not cancel the service operation; the controller may complete normally when the service response arrives.

## 8. Cache Line and Addressing Constraints

The cache line data width must be 128 bits. Each line contains two 64-bit data words, and the requested word is selected using the word-select address bit.

The controller treats addresses at or above the configured cacheable start address as cacheable, unless global bypass mode is active. Addresses below that boundary are non-cacheable and must use the bypass path.

# Miss Handler Behavioral Specification

## 1. Functional Overview

The miss handler manages all cache misses for a set-associative data cache. It accepts memory requests from multiple request ports and separates them into two classes:

- **Bypass requests**: single-beat accesses that do not allocate or modify cache state.
- **Miss requests**: cacheable accesses that require a cache-line refill, and possibly a writeback of a dirty evicted line.

The module provides two independent AXI master paths:

- a **bypass path** for single-beat bypass transactions, and
- a **refill/writeback path** for cache-line fills and dirty-line writebacks.

The module is also responsible for:

- selecting cache lines for allocation and eviction,
- writing back dirty lines before they are replaced,
- initializing the cache status storage after reset,
- flushing and invalidating the cache on command.

## 2. Reset and Initialization

After reset is released and before normal operation begins, the module shall initialize the cache status storage. It must sweep all cache sets and clear every valid and dirty indication. After initialization, all cache lines are invalid and clean.

While this initialization sweep is in progress:

- the module shall not start a new miss operation,
- the module shall not start a flush operation,
- bypass requests may still be handled independently.

## 3. Request Handling and Arbitration

Each request port can present a memory request with attributes such as:

- valid indication,
- read/write direction,
- address,
- write data,
- byte strobes,
- size,
- bypass qualifier.

A request qualified as a bypass request shall be handled on the bypass path and shall never cause a cache line to be allocated, refilled, or invalidated.

A request not qualified as bypass is a miss request. The module shall handle one miss at a time. While a miss is outstanding:

- the port whose miss is being served shall be indicated as active,
- new miss requests from other ports shall not be granted,
- the active port shall remain active until its cache line has been refilled or otherwise resolved.

If several bypass requests arrive in the same cycle, the module shall select one for service and provide a grant to the selected port only. The identity of the selected request must be preserved so that the corresponding read data or write completion response is returned only to the originating port.

A flush request, when it is able to start, takes precedence over starting a new miss operation.

## 4. Bypass Transaction Behavior

For a bypass request, the module shall:

1. Issue the request on the bypass AXI interface as a single-beat transaction.
2. Preserve the address, data, byte strobes, size, and direction of the request.
3. For a read, return the read data to the requesting port when the transaction completes.
4. For a write, send the write data and byte strobes, and return a completion response to the requesting port when the write transaction completes.

Bypass transactions shall not modify any cache metadata or cache data storage.

The bypass path shall continue to operate independently while miss handling or flush operations are in progress.

## 5. Miss Handling Behavior

### 5.1 Miss Acceptance

When a miss request is accepted, the module shall capture the request attributes needed to service the miss:

- which port requested the miss,
- the miss address,
- whether the access is a read or a write,
- write data and byte strobes if it is a write.

The module shall not accept another miss until the current miss has been fully resolved.

### 5.2 Set Lookup and Way Selection

For the set indexed by the miss address, the module shall examine the status of all ways.

If at least one way in the set is invalid, the module shall select an invalid way for the refill.

If all ways are valid, the module shall select a victim way using a pseudo-random replacement policy:

- If the selected victim is clean, it may be overwritten directly.
- If the selected victim is dirty, the module shall first write the entire dirty line back to memory. After the writeback is accepted, the way shall be invalidated. The module shall then re-examine the set and allocate the now-invalid way for the new line.

### 5.3 Cache-Line Refill

Once a target way is known, the module shall issue a cache-line read request for the miss address to the refill AXI interface. The address used for the refill shall be the cache-line-aligned address of the missing line.

The module shall indicate a miss grant to the port being served when the refill request is accepted.

When the refill data returns, the module shall:

- store the complete cache line into the selected way,
- set the tag of the selected way to the tag of the miss address,
- set the valid indication of the selected way,
- leave the dirty indication cleared for a read miss.

### 5.4 Write Miss Handling

If the original miss request was a write, the module shall merge the captured write bytes into the refilled cache line at the byte offset indicated by the miss address.

After the write data is merged:

- the line shall be marked dirty,
- the selected way shall remain valid,
- the write is considered complete.

### 5.5 Critical Word Delivery

The module shall provide the word that caused the miss on a dedicated output as soon as that word is received from the refill AXI path. A valid strobe shall accompany this output.

This critical-word delivery may occur before the entire cache line has been stored. It allows the requesting side to proceed without waiting for the full line refill to complete.

## 6. Writeback Behavior

When a dirty cache line must be evicted, the module shall write the entire line back to its home memory address.

The writeback shall include:

- the full dirty line data,
- byte strobes asserted for the entire line,
- the correct memory address formed from the line tag and set index.

Once the AXI side accepts the writeback, the module shall invalidate the written-back way. The valid and dirty indications for that way shall be cleared.

Writebacks may occur:

- as part of a miss when the selected victim is dirty,
- as part of a flush when dirty lines remain in a set being flushed.

## 7. Cache Status Maintenance

The module is responsible for updating the valid and dirty status of cache ways through its cache memory port.

The module shall ensure that:

- a way is never marked valid before its refill data is written,
- a dirty way is never invalidated without first issuing its writeback,
- a clean way marked for replacement can be made invalid without a writeback,
- refill writes preserve all data in other ways of the same set,
- status writes do not corrupt unrelated cache metadata.

## 8. Aliasing and Address Match Indication

For every request port, the module shall provide an address-match indication that compares the address presented by that port with the address of the currently outstanding miss.

The match comparison shall use only the cache-line portion of the address and shall ignore the byte offset within the line.

A port shall receive a match indication when its address is within the same cache line as the outstanding miss, regardless of whether the port is the one currently being served.

When no miss is outstanding, no port shall receive a match indication.

## 9. Flush Behavior

A flush request shall cause the module to make the entire cache coherent by:

- writing back every dirty line,
- invalidating all lines,
- leaving the cache in an invalid and clean state.

The flush operation shall not start while the cache is reported busy. If a flush request is asserted while the module is busy, the module shall wait until the busy condition is removed before beginning the flush.

While flushing:

- new miss requests shall not be accepted,
- the module shall sweep every cache set,
- for each set, if any dirty way exists, the module shall write back one dirty way, invalidate it, and repeat until no dirty ways remain,
- when no dirty way remains in the current set, the module shall invalidate all valid ways in that set and move to the next set.

When the flush has processed the last set, the module shall assert the flush acknowledgment. At that point all cache lines shall be invalid and clean.

## 10. Miss Event Output

The module shall provide a miss-event output that indicates when a cache miss is being handled. This output is intended for performance monitoring and does not affect data-path behavior.

## 11. Summary of Interface Behavior

From the perspective of its external ports, the module must provide:

- a bypass AXI master path that completes single-beat read and write transactions and returns responses to the correct request port,
- a refill/writeback AXI master path that performs cache-line reads and dirty-line writes,
- per-port grants for bypass and miss transactions,
- per-port active-miss indications,
- per-port address-match indications,
- critical-word data and valid indication for miss refills,
- flush request handling and flush completion acknowledgment,
- miss-event indication,
- a cache memory port for reading and updating cache data and status.

The module shall satisfy all of these behaviors without requiring external assistance beyond the AXI interfaces, the cache memory port, and the control inputs it is given.
